# FDG9115

> DO mark generic type parameters on generic delegates as covariant when the type parameter is used as output, but not input, and your language supports creating covariant types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.8.2 Covariance.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9115
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Mark the type parameter '{0}' of the delegate '{1}' as covariant (out); it is only used as output

Library only: as for FDG9111, changing a released delegate is a breaking change (FDG9116 body). The text has no body of its own. FDG9115 reports an invariant type parameter of an externally visible generic delegate that appears only in output positions of its signature, as for FDG9111. A type parameter that is not used at all could take either modifier and is not reported, and neither is one that a static member uses, so coverage is partial. Adding the modifier changes the declaration of a public type and can make existing conversions and overload resolutions ambiguous, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
